datasets: 311 Customer Service Requests 2025 (data/311_2025.csv, bundled but unused by default -year 2024)
data/sample/*.csv real-row subsets built by tools/mksample
concurrency_primitives: goroutines; two files ingested concurrently (sync.WaitGroup); generic parallel[T] ingest with reader -> bounded batch channel (2000 rows, cap workers*2) -> NumCPU workers with worker-local partials -> merge; BuildParallel join splits slices into NumCPU chunks each filling a private Dataset, merged once via channel; -verify asserts parallel join == sequential join with reflect.DeepEqual; analyses sequential
design_patterns: Strategy (analysis.Analyzer interface with 5 implementations, All() registry); explicit 3-stage pipeline in main; sequential reference implementations (Build, ReadCrime) verified against parallel versions; no Builder/Factory
questions: Which neighborhoods rank high in BOTH Part 1 crime and 311 demand? (Mayor's Office)
Do sanitation/blight 311 requests track violent crime across neighborhoods? (DPW)
Which neighborhoods have high crime but low 311 use, suggesting under-reporting? (BPD)
How do crime, street-lighting requests and transportation requests vary by hour of day? (DOT)
What are the monthly crime and 311 trends, and which neighborhoods diverge from the citywide crime pattern? (Planning)
overview: Compact multi-package Go module (cmd, internal/{ingest,join,analysis,normalize,model,report}, tools/mksample) with a generic batch-ingest worker pool and a chunked parallel join, each paired with a sequential reference implementation that tests and a -verify flag prove equivalent. An Analyzer Strategy interface drives five plain-text ASCII reports. Code is readable with good thread-safety comments, tests in four packages and a macOS CI workflow, but memory handling is naive (all records retained with un-interned strings; 830 MB RSS) and the report layer is minimal.
stakeholder_value: Q3's under-reporting z-score (Inner Harbor, Dunbar-Broadway, Canton Industrial Area) with join-gap neighborhoods separated out is genuinely actionable for BPD/311 outreach, and Q2's r=0.68 blight-violence association is useful context for DPW. Q1 is a size-biased rank-sum of raw counts, while Q4 (hourly histograms) and Q5 (monthly trend, crime-only divergence) place the datasets side by side rather than joining them, so about half the questions deliver real cross-dataset insight.
issues: LATE submission (filename contained _LATE_); flagged, not deducted
Memory: every kept record retained with un-interned CSV substrings; 830 MB RSS and 2.8 GB total allocation on full data; no memory design documented
Q4 and Q5 are largely single-dataset views presented side by side rather than cross-dataset joins
data/311_2025.csv (379 MB) is bundled but never used by the default run
Analyses run sequentially; ASCII-only output with 29-char label truncation; README ends mid-sentence
rationale: Full credit for a clean build, three real bundled datasets, and a complete two-second run on 950 MB of data with verified parallel/sequential equivalence and no races. Concurrency (14) and architecture (14) are near the top thanks to real worker pools, tests and CI. Memory scores 6 because beyond streaming reads the design retains everything with no interning and no documented thought, and stakeholder scores 10 because two of five questions are not truly cross-dataset. Total 88, B; late flag noted without deduction.
